# Vaultor: living codebase and agent guide

Last reviewed: 2026-10-24. This is the current implementation reference. Update it in every change as required by [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). Historical specifications are context only. See [API.md](development/API.md), [OPERATIONS.md](development/OPERATIONS.md), and the [documentation index](README.md).

## Product and architecture

## Vaultor is a personal, locally hosted knowledge workspace. Notes and uploaded files are resources, organized by nested collections and tags and connected through inline links. The desktop restores its selected server/workspace, starting the owned server when needed; browser access uses a local owner handoff or host-approved LAN device session. There are no accounts, master passwords, note lock controls, note/archive encryption, or encrypted archive compatibility. D5 adds owner/device access credentials separately from workspace data. Obsolete credentials stored in an existing database are ignored; startup does not delete resources.

React 19 + TypeScript 5.9 + Vite 8 + Tailwind 3 + Redux + Tiptap 3 call Spring Boot 4 / Java 25 through a shared Axios client at /api. Spring Data JPA stores metadata and serialized Tiptap documents in SQLite; file bytes live separately on disk. Hikari uses one connection per workspace to serialize application transactions and avoid concurrent SQLite read-to-write lock upgrades; reads also queue, so keep transactions short. W1 adds up to eight isolated host workspaces: the adopted default uses the main context; each additional workspace uses a separate database/file root and independent Spring domain/JPA/worker context in the same JVM. Explicit X-Vaultor-Workspace routing never changes a global active datasource. [WORKSPACES.md](architecture/WORKSPACES.md) owns catalog, grants, migration/checkpoint, API and bounds. Backend JSON uses Jackson 3 tools.jackson. Exact versions are in the package lock and pom.xml. Vite proxies /api and /access to 127.0.0.1:8080 on fixed port 5173; only exact loopback development Origins are rewritten. Docker embeds the frontend in the Spring JAR and serves one origin.

The backend is authoritative. This is not an offline browser database or a synchronization system. Docker publishes to loopback by default. Host-approved LAN access is explicit and off by default; never expose this personal deployment publicly or bypass device approval for debugging.

## Agent-owned release delivery

Installed-app changes are not complete at a development build: agents own version/package-lock bumps, fresh UI plus embedded browser/server builds, focused/native target checks, original-key-signed artifact pairs, source commits/tags, GitHub draft assets and publication under [RELEASE-PROCESS.md](desktop/RELEASE-PROCESS.md). The user-facing exact Windows/Mac/browser/Docker/Ubuntu status and update steps are in [INSTALLATION-AND-UPDATES.md](desktop/INSTALLATION-AND-UPDATES.md). Documentation/test-only changes with no shipped behavior do not require installers. `desktop/scripts/release-artifacts.mjs` verifies installer identity/size/checksum; `publish-release.mjs` defaults to dry-run and requires a clean source tree and matching pushed tag for draft upload, preserving existing assets. Explicit --add-platform permits a missing verified platform pair on an existing published release and byte-identical retries; differing assets are rejected, and the original source tag remains immutable. It does not certify native validation or publish a draft automatically. GitHub Releases are the default public update source. Updates checks on opening and once after normal installed startup, selecting the highest stable complete per-platform pair from at most 100 records. Bounded credential-free GitHub asset redirects are supported; custom feeds still reject redirects. Installed Windows uses one Update and restart action, verified download/save/backup, a hidden parent-waiting silent installer helper and relaunch. Manual import is Advanced; development/portable/Mac replacement remains explicitly manual. No CI key storage or paid feed is configured. Missing native Mac access/original key/verification must be reported, not presented as a successful release.

## Current platform responsibilities and compatibility

Reviewed against integrated master and the published Windows 0.18.1 / Android alpha.28 baseline on 2026-10-24. W1–W3 and R1–R10 engineering is complete. Linked Markdown editing has separately authorized, isolated [Gate 1 engineering](development/qualification/LINKED-MARKDOWN-G1.md); no linked-source feature is shipped. Other future product work requires separate authorization. [The deferred roadmap](plans/future-roadmap.md) distinguishes limitations, pending platform acceptance and future ideas. [Qualification evidence](development/qualification/R10.md) records actual measurements and tests, not new requirements.

| Surface | Responsibility and current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Host (Spring/SQLite) | Authoritative originals, revisions, workspace generations, grants, conversion, receipts, synced Reviews and coherent exports/checkpoints. Eight bounded isolated workspace contexts in one JVM; no global active datasource. |
| Desktop (Electron) | Owns its bundled loopback host, native files, protected connections, updates and independent local copies. Can also use a paired remote host; client installation never updates that remote host. |
| Browser | Same shared API/editor, sessions and recovery; a client of its selected host, without a local authoritative database or Java host. |
| Android | Source-bound connected/offline reader, immutable Review capture/delivery, confirmed new-input imports and full/partial exports. React Native UI/motion, thin Kotlin transport/storage/platform modules and restricted reader/media DOM. No original document/organization/lifecycle writes, host administration or independent writable workspace. |

Current API/minimum-client protocol is **3/3**; companion checkpoint schema **1**; updater envelope **1**; flat portable archives **5**, flat partial packages **6**; hierarchy-bearing full/partial packages **7/8**. Release versions are independent of protocol/schema versions. Hosts read older full archives 1–5 and hierarchy7; partial6/8 merges or imports into an empty new workspace, never replaces populated data. Capability checks additionally gate Reviews, checkpoints, collected imports and export operations. Mac arm64 0.13.0 is the last published Mac build and lacks Reviews/archive4–6; no current integrated Mac installer is qualified. Windows 0.18.1 is published as a non-Latest Windows-only release; Android alpha.28/code32 is unchanged by R10. See [installation](desktop/INSTALLATION-AND-UPDATES.md) and [Mac qualification](desktop/MAC-HANDOFF.md).

[WORKSPACES.md](architecture/WORKSPACES.md) owns identity/isolation/adoption/grants. [PLATFORM.md](architecture/PLATFORM.md) owns transport/cancellation/capability boundaries; [DESKTOP.md](desktop/DESKTOP.md) owns native host/process/storage lifecycle, and [MULTI-DEVICE.md](architecture/MULTI-DEVICE.md) owns approved saved-change streams. Fixed-default legacy routing is never a mutable active workspace. Independent copies are forks with new workspace identity, not bidirectional synchronization. Credentials/catalogs/device journals never enter portable archives.

Use small coherent direct commits on master under [AI_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md](development/AI_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md); isolation requires a reason. Preserve protections, immutable release tags and approved presentation contracts. Do not incorporate another active AI branch without explicit integration authorization.

[PRIMARY-TEST-WORKSPACE.md](development/PRIMARY-TEST-WORKSPACE.md) owns marked Small70/Atlas5000 fixtures, protected API generation and guarded reset. Historical [baseline](development/ATLAS-BASELINE.md), [file-search measurements](development/FILE-SEARCH-MEASUREMENTS.md), [scale results](development/SCALE-INTEGRATION.md) and [R10 evidence](development/qualification/R10.md) retain sample conditions and limits. Never point fixture tools at personal data, publish profiles, or run two owners against one database.

### Host companion checkpoints

Host0.11.0 advertises companionSnapshots:1 at unchanged protocol3/archive3. [COMPANIONS.md](architecture/COMPANIONS.md) owns the source-bound dataset/API contract. CompanionSnapshots/CompanionController implement generation/device-bound durable receipts, bounded selection estimates, coherent private immutable note/file/organization captures, paged inventory/coverage and checkpoint comparison, hashed payloads and single-range byte resume. Whole manifest bytes are downloadable and SHA-verifiable. This is not archive ZIP export, a write queue or Android offline storage; Android R4 consumes it through the native retained store described below; R5 host triage is complete; R6 A0–A5 engineering is integrated below, with physical acceptance pending; R7–R9 are published on master; R10 quality/scale/upgrade engineering is integrated.

One worker per workspace captures under its exclusive WorkspaceGate/SQLite transaction. Existing resource/organization/Trash/Restore/import requests cannot mix metadata and bytes. Other workspaces are independent. Companions routes participate in workspace authorization and private stop/drain, without retaining a request EntityManager/SQLite connection during network writes. The shared host catalog is explicitly registered in child contexts for grant rechecks. HostFiles' atomic private-file helper is public for domain artifact use; no keys/credentials are stored in checkpoints.

Limits: four active checkpoints/128 receipts; one-hour fixed byte lifetime/seven-day receipts;10,000 resources and collections/tags;100 seed IDs;64MiB per original,1MiB per note,64MiB JSON/manifest;2GiB retained payloads per workspace plus bounded metadata. Oversized/missing/policy-omitted originals and unselected links are explicit. Partial preparation fails/cancels without READY; restart removes interrupted staging. Damaged optional storage disables companion downloads with503, without disabling original-workspace startup. Immutable streams hold a maintenance read lease; every byte chunk rechecks current access/generation/cancellation; If-Match pins manifests and client final hashes reject truncation. Deltas compare two matching immutable selections; expired/gapped streams require full reconciliation, never silently broader scope. Current validation/publication evidence is recorded in desktop/releases/v0.11.0.md.

The R10 host0.16.1 caches one reclaimable immutable parsed manifest per workspace when its serialized bytes are at most4MiB to avoid re-deserializing an Atlas manifest for every payload. Current bytes are still read and SHA-256-verified on every request after receipt/source/validator checks; cached authority is never admitted. Cancellation/expiry/shutdown clear the matching parsed value, and larger manifests keep the verified parse path. [COMPANIONS.md](architecture/COMPANIONS.md) owns the exact boundary; [R10 qualification](development/qualification/R10.md) owns baseline/candidate measurements and acceptance status. Protocol/schema/Android app remain unchanged.

### Exports, connections and updates

The published baseline is Androidalpha.28/code32 and compatible Windows0.18.1; R10 and desktop Open Notes are retained, with nested collections/folder imports now published for Windows. Full connected exports use archive5 for flat or7 for nested organization and host note-format converters. Portable partial6/8 packages contain checksum-covered inventory/omissions/dependency depth and Review/import-provenance coverage; merge or empty-new import only, never populated replacement. Offline verified checkpoints support partial/Markdown+available originals and exact JSON sidecars, with hidden provenance/all-host Review omissions declared. Separate native derivative export storage is256MiB/eight operations; captured source/generation/UUID survive active-source changes and process death. Save/Share verify bytes again and require Android/provider consent; ordinary exports never contain credentials or unacknowledged queues. [Export contract](android/EXPORTS-AND-CONNECTIONS.md) owns exact bounds and compatibility.

Existing Settings & tools/source management gain utility sheets, optional bounded permission-aware NSD candidates and identity-checked address updates. Native APK updates use bounded official release metadata/downloads, apksig cryptographic validation, original signer/package/increasing code/signed compatibility, private staging and explicit OS consent. Metadata/checksums alone never establish authenticity. Independent journals leave R6/R7 downloads, Reviews/imports and legacy recovery intact. No silent install, force-stopped delivery, fourth primary destination or Android host administration.

## Android delivery

Mobile-only releases follow [ANDROID.md](android/ANDROID.md), original APK signer, monotonic versionCode and immutable android/v tags. Never rebuild desktop for Android-only changes or access/pair the user's phone; explicit emulator serials only. Android uses safe mobile/reader DOM rendering without editable Tiptap, the Home/Library/Review folio, source selection and temporary previews. Reader controls provide device-local reading controls, outline/find, revision-checked positions and full-screen media. Original-resource API writes remain refused; recency POST remains admitted; original note/organization/lifecycle/image-placement writes remain retired.

[READER.md](android/READER.md) owns current rendering/recovery details. Legacy encrypted drafts, uncertain receipts, creation/lifecycle identities and pending media bytes remain intact. Dedicated Legacy recovery exports readable Markdown, original structured JSON and retained media to a private ZIP through Android SAF, without credentials or overwriting host content. Reconnect/background/switching never replay writes or acknowledge recovery. The legacy saved cache (12 notes/8MiB) remains separate from R4 retained downloads. R5 host review triage is complete; A3 adds local capture below, while Android Review delivery/status is implemented in R6 A4; imports and exports are published in the integrated R7–R9 release. [Android UI philosophy](design/ANDROID_UI_PHILOSOPHY.md) governs the current companion direction. R2 implements reading refinements; its actual publication checks are in android/releases/0.1.0-alpha.10.md. API36/37 Windows emulators are agent-owned; Samsung S24 Ultra/OneUI8.5–9 acceptance is user-owned.

### Reader presentation and media

ReadingProvider in mobile/src/ui.ts owns normalized device-only OS/Light/Dark/OLED, accents, text size/spacing/measure and Snappy/Smooth. ReadingControls presents flat native controls with retained choices and Retry. Native readerPreferences uses separate private SharedPreferences; it never enters archives/recovery. OLED is black; Dark is neutral #101114; OS follows the current system. CSS token updates and literal cross-mark find retain document nodes/selection. A2 removes decorative new-visit fading; contextual media Fit uses shared structure timing, while reduced motion retains immediate endpoints. Tables/code scroll within their blocks. Outline is bounded256headings; find200characters/500matches; the DOM renderer bounds traversal at20,000nodes/64depth and shows limits/unknown content without modifying original JSON.

ReaderView/WorkspaceScreen own typed load/source tickets, native sheet/Back ownership, confirmed HTTP(S) external opening and block/revision-based restoration. Distinct link cycles retain separate positions within the200visit journey; files never advance it. Returning from browsing/previews restores the mounted reader. Explicit browsing invalidates pending linked navigation; hidden readers cannot overwrite positions with clamped offsets. Native Action labels are noninteractive children so the owning Pressable reliably receives taps after sheets close.

ResourcePreview uses a native full-screen window and restricted local media WebView (reader/media.*), authenticated source-bound originals, Fit/Actual size/zoom1–4, pan/pinch and source-note image gallery (128unique IDs). Media has a fixed scroll viewport and browser zoom is disabled; enlarged pixels never redefine their own fit viewport on Android17. PDF rendering is page-at-a-time,20MiB input/100,000pages/max2560×4000pixels with preserved aspect/white paper; password/unsupported failures remain actionable. Images sample to2048edge,20MiB/40MP; original Save/Share/Copy/Open with retain bytes/colors. Encrypted readerMedia metadata retains page/zoom/pan for100source-scoped resources; previews do not reopen on restart. Text preview100KB and transport64MiB remain. This is evictable reading metadata, not offline downloads. No HTTP/schema/protocol/archive/desktop change. See READER.md and MEDIA.md for authoritative bounds.

build-release.ps1 now requires TypeScript before signing. test-reading.ps1 accepts only explicit emulator-5554/5556 and a disposable loopback fixture; ordered native cases fail fast. Exact release-byte verification and publication evidence belong in android/releases/0.1.0-alpha.10.md. Current integrated qualification is in development/qualification/R10.md; physical acceptance remains unqualified.

### Android retained reading

Android alpha.11/versionCode15 adds VaultorCompanions (private SQLite schema3 + retained payload files), OfflineControls and a narrow native snapshot adapter. Verification/activation, resume, quotas, source locking and plaintext-private storage threat model are authoritative in [OFFLINE.md](android/OFFLINE.md). Native queries page/filter/count downloaded metadata and saved note text without enumerating resources into JS. No host/database resource schema/protocol/archive/desktop change. Appearance is reachable from navigation and Workspaces; shortcut requests use an independent channel and Pinned is admitted by the native GET allowlist. Code scroll backgrounds contain long lines; inline code wraps. Initial content mounting waits for coherent session restoration, with stable screen keys so fast local loads do not lose the native reader subtree. R4 release evidence lives in android/releases/0.1.0-alpha.11.md.

### Review evidence and triage

[Windows 0.14.0 release notes](desktop/releases/v0.14.0.md) retain desktop redesign/Review integration and installed-upgrade evidence. Current Review behavior is owned by the topic guide below.

ReviewService/ReviewController add isolated review_items storage, idempotent UUID evidence, generation admission, conditional review-status revisions and reviews change invalidation. Original documents/revisions remain separate. ReviewInbox/ReviewButton adapt workspace/resource triage into the current redesigned SidebarFrame, NoteOrientation and PreviewShell action rows. AppModal/dialogFocus own containment and trigger restoration; successful guarded navigation closes the inbox before handing focus to the destination. Review status failures remain local, with background diagnostics instead of the unrelated Retry saves banner. Zero-count entries use an accessible compact icon; positive counts stay visible. Existing geometry, compression, motion and theme primitives remain authoritative. [REVIEWS.md](workspace/REVIEWS.md) owns bounds, missing/changed evidence and integration contracts. R5 introduced archive4 with reviews; current full transfers use archive5/7 with hidden original provenance, importing1–8; scoped note packages include reviews.json, with standalone document presentation unchanged. Protocol3 remains; Android capture and automatic delivery are implemented. R5 Windows0.12.0 is published; native Mac gate remains pending.

### Android Review and interaction architecture

React Native owns product UI and motion; thin Kotlin owns protected storage/transport, platform presentation and semantic haptic policy. [Shell navigation](android/SHELL-NAVIGATION.md), [reader context](android/READER-CONTEXT.md) and [interaction foundations](android/INTERACTION-FOUNDATIONS.md) own retained-reader geometry, resource-origin motion, contextual Aa/settings, theme/system bars, Back/IME and reduced-motion endpoints. Correctness never waits for animation. Ordinary navigation, Find, accent changes and automatic synchronization are silent; standard H2 marks meaningful evidence/source locks and REVIEW_CAPTURED is the sole authored product completion. The [Android design contract](design/ANDROID_UI_PHILOSOPHY.md) governs future UI changes.

[Review capture](android/REVIEW-CAPTURE.md) freezes host/workspace/generation/resource/revision, quote/context and validated block/one-based PDF locator. A separate encrypted format1 AtomicFile journal protects up to256 items/8MiB independently of evictable downloads. Flag opens a protected draft; typing does not publish. One Create Review waits for protection and atomically queues the same UUID/body. Keep draft/Back never completes it; failed writes retain prior evidence.

[Review delivery](android/REVIEW-SYNC.md) has one native owner: captured-source pinned TLS/grant/generation/capability admission, durable sending before PUT, exact full-body retries after unknown outcomes and validated persisted receipts. GET status rechecks generation. Queue commit/resume/reconnect drive foreground delivery; desktop status is separate from local durability. Background events cannot activate or retarget a source. Revocation/replacement retains protected evidence and locks retained source content. No Android status-write UI or guaranteed suspended/force-stopped delivery.

Install signed APK updates over existing alphas without uninstalling/clearing data. Legacy recovery remains private and never replays retired original writes. Historical [R6 qualification](development/qualification/R6.md) and [R7–R9 qualification](development/qualification/R7-R9.md) retain genuine upgrade/source-lock evidence; [R10](development/qualification/R10.md) owns final integrated measurements. Physical Samsung/haptics/TalkBack/OEM/real-LAN and current Mac acceptance remain unclaimed.

## Data model and persistence

| Entity | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Resource / resources | UUID string id, type note/file, title, serialized content, filePath, MIME, size, createdAt/updatedAt/lastOpenedAt, favorite, internal optimistic revision_number/revision_seed, nullable trashed_at/purge_pending/trash_organization, many-to-many tags and collections |
| Review / review_items | Generation-scoped immutable evidence, target/provenance, open/resolved/dismissed status, private review validator; no resource cascade; portable representation in REVIEWS.md |
| ResourceCollection / collections | UUID id, nullable parentId, display name, unique parent-scoped normalized_name key, favorite, internal creationFingerprint for retry-safe creation; resource_collections joins resources to multiple collections |
| Tag / tags | UUID id, normalized unique name, persistent color |
| Relationship / relationships | fromId/toId/type=link, derived from resourceLink and image nodes; IDs are plain strings |
| Setting / settings | key_name/value; app_settings_v2 holds workspace/local/keybindings |
| resource_fts | Derived SQLite FTS5 resource titles/visible saved-note and extracted supported file text; resource triggers maintain transactional consistency; startup/Diagnostics rebuild in gated batches |
| file_search | Derived bounded saved-file text/status/hash keyed by resource version and workspace generation; subprocess decoding, no archive inclusion |
| LifecycleRequest | Durable per-item operation ID/resource/action/expected revision/result, including irreversible purge cleanup and completed purge tombstones; nonportable |
| TransferOperation | persisted kind, status, phase, progress, mode, detail, requestId, timestamps, cleanup journal |

SQLite uses Hibernate ddl-auto=update with hibernate.hbm2ddl.jdbc_metadata_extraction_strategy=individually; there is no versioned migration framework. Individual inspection is required because existing SQLite FTS5/shadow tables expose untyped columns that crash Hibernate grouped metadata extraction on restart. Keep schema updates enabled and leave the derived search tables/data intact. Resource DTOs omit internal file paths and expose note content as a JSON object (never a JSON-encoded string). Entity persistence still stores content as text. Dates use LocalDateTime without a timezone suffix. Opening a resource updates only lastOpenedAt through a metadata SQL write; it does not change updatedAt or hydrate/save its document. Some tag mutations can still change updatedAt, so it is not strictly a content timestamp. Import preserves archived IDs on replacement and allocates new IDs on merge.

ResourceService saves the note and rebuilds outgoing link relationships transactionally. LinkExtractionService extracts resourceLink/image attrs.resourceId; table sourceResourceId is checked/remapped by DocumentService but is not a backlink edge. The former replace-links-and-delete and hard-delete routes are retired (405). Trash retains incoming labels and placements without rewriting referring notes; permanent deletion runs only through revision-checked durable cleanup in Trash. The read-only integrity API reports missing targets. Tag names trim/lowercase and unify case-insensitively; default colors are deterministic. FileStorageService confines paths to its configured directory.

## Backend and API contracts

Use [API.md](development/API.md) for flows and /api/openapi.json for the machine contract. The same APIs serve agents and UI, without a privileged execution interface. Explicit DTOs cover resources, tags, settings and operations. List responses include items/page/size/totalItems/totalPages (size 1–200). Browsing returns metadata-only summaries with title/collection/type/all-selected-tags/favorites filters and recent/updated/title sorting. GET /resources/query supplies relevance-ranked saved note/title/supported PDF and UTF-8 file search with scoped coverage with metadata and safe snippets (size 1–100); legacy /resources/search still caps title matches at 50. See SEARCH.md for search/index contracts. GET resource detail supplies document content. Resource details and list summaries include collections [{id,name}]; list enrichment batches tags and collections without reading documents. PUT /resources/{id}/favorite persists a boolean without changing modification time. GET /organization/pins pages mixed shortcuts with optional kind filtering and appliedKind acknowledgment, batching optional resource summaries; POST /organization/selection reads membership counts for selected IDs. PUT /collections/creations/{id} creates once with initial members, and optional collectionId on note creation/file imports assigns membership transactionally. See [Library workflows](workspace/LIBRARY.md).

Resource details expose an opaque revision; the UI sends quoted If-Match on note updates, returning 412 NOTE_REVISION_CONFLICT for stale writes. JPA optimistic locking guards concurrent updates. GET /workspace/identity returns persistent identity/replacement generation; generation changes inside the replacement transaction. Internal identifiers are excluded from portable archives.

All API responses carry X-Request-ID. Errors use problem details with status, code, detail, fieldErrors and requestId. Default logs contain request method/path/status/duration and mutation outcomes, not complete request payloads, note bodies or binary contents. Unexpected failures include stack traces. Frontend boundaries and network errors retain diagnostic references and correlate server request IDs.

D1 capabilities explicitly expose serverBuild, apiProtocolVersion and minimumClientProtocolVersion; current protocol and minimum client protocol are 3 for managed-image editing and safe resource lifecycle operations. Old clients are refused before editor mounting; update both client and host. BuildInformation uses BUILD_VERSION (default desktop-d1) consistently for capabilities/health and request/transfer logs. The client uses VITE_BUILD_VERSION separately. Deploy frontend/backend together; the UI intentionally rejects old servers lacking compatibility metadata before mounting settings/workspace. Details and examples: [API.md](development/API.md).

RequestLoggingFilter supplies correlation/logging around HostAccessFilter. Only approved requests reach WorkspaceRequestFilter's shared gate for resource/tag/settings/collection/organization calls. Transfers take the exclusive gate during snapshot/commit and search rebuild takes it per batch of 100, and concurrent approved calls receive 409 WORKSPACE_BUSY. The gate is process-local: run a single backend against a data directory. Health requires approval and reports readiness/busy state; integrity checks never repair data. Compose rotates JSON logs at three 10 MiB files; desktop logs retain their existing bounded ring/disk rotation.

## Workspace transfer and export foundation

Individual note export format buttons immediately save the target note, prepare an immutable export and automatically request its download. Dashboard keeps NoteExportModal and its NoteExportController mounted independently of picker visibility; the picker closes automatically after download handoff, with Download again retained in a compact status card. One active/unresolved export at a time prevents duplicate clicks. Bounded status retries and download retries retain the operation; confirmed preparation failure or a definite pre-operation graph conflict offers a fresh save/snapshot attempt. Ambiguous creation failures require inspection rather than automatic resubmission. Download again is available, conversion warnings and IDs are disclosures, and no browser-save success is claimed. Reload stops frontend tracking; it does not replay old downloads. Workspace identity/generation changes dispose the export controller; import closes stale export/title UI. See NOTE-EXPORTS.md for lifecycle and limitations.

TransferService orchestrates one persisted-operation worker. WorkspaceExporter separates archive rendering; ExporterRegistry enables workspace/zip and notes/md, md-assets, pdf, docx. Scope definitions also reserve notes and table. DocumentService validates node/mark shapes separately from attribute objects (ordered lists legitimately have attrs.type=null) and traverses blocks, marks, links, tables and asset reference attributes; renderers consume structured documents, not editor HTML. NoteExporter registrations and NoteRenderer implement standalone and outgoing-graph export; see [NOTE-EXPORTS.md](workspace/NOTE-EXPORTS.md) for API, fidelity and limits.

Note export defaults to This note; Include linked resources previews counts, saves only participants, and validates the final graph fingerprint under the mutation gate. NoteExportGraph follows recognized structured outgoing references breadth-first, deduplicates cycles, excludes backlinks and bounds nodes/depth/document-and-binary bytes. Changed membership after saving requires review. Graph Markdown is a ZIP of relative-linked note files; PDF/Word use combined sections and internal destinations/bookmarks, packaged with original files when present. Reading content uses labels rather than resource UUIDs; optional references identify omissions, while export.json carries package traceability. Reading packages are distinct from workspace archives. No document/database/session schema changed. See NOTE-EXPORTS for precise limits, contracts and known fidelity restrictions.

Flat ZIP version 5 (hierarchy-bearing version 7) contains checksum-covered originals/{resource-id} and per-note importOriginal provenance in addition to manifest.json (version, creation time, counts, SHA-256 checksums), workspace.json (logical resources including Trash/timestamps/restoration labels, tags/workspace settings plus organization: collections, memberships and resource/collection favorites, plus required portable reviews), and files/{resource-id}. Archive1–8 remain readable; older-version archives with unsupported reviews/provenance, orphan original entries and future versions fail safely. Original ownership remaps with notes on merge; purge removes associated originals, while edits and Trash/Restore retain them. No live SQLite file, credentials, diagnostics or device appearance/keybindings are exported. JSON entries cap at 20 MiB, archive defaults to 512 MiB, expanded data 2 GiB and 20,000 entries. Configure limits through environment variables; malformed paths, duplicate entries, checksums, counts and document/reference shapes are validated before mutation. Missing document targets appear as preview warnings.

Preview stages the upload. Merge generates a new resource graph and rewrites both inline links and table source IDs; same-name tags reuse existing colors and workspace settings stay unchanged. Replace requires explicit confirmation and replaces resources/tags/files/reviews/workspace settings while retaining local appearance and keybindings. Both derive backlinks from documents. Merge remaps collection members to newly allocated resource IDs, unifies collections by normalized sibling name beneath remapped parents and preserves existing collection favorites. Replace restores archived collection IDs and all favorites. Organization validates before mutation and restores within the metadata transaction. Plain version 1 archives remain readable without organization. Repeating a commit returns the original operation, never applies twice; to retry a failed commit upload/preview again.

Before the DB transaction, imported binaries are copied under unique names and their names journaled. Metadata changes and the obsolete-file cleanup journal commit in one transaction. Old binaries are deleted only after commit. Restart marks interrupted queued/running operations failed and removes unreferenced staging; CLEANUP resumes idempotently. Rollback preserves existing metadata and binaries. Cancellation is allowed at preview/queue and during import preparation, but never after the commit phase begins. Progress is phase-based, not byte-level. UI refreshes after completion without timed reload or backend exit.

Future work: table XLSX/PDF and separately connected Google Docs publishing. Individual note Markdown/PDF/DOCX export is implemented. Do not expose unfinished formats as selectable. Artifact/staging directories currently remain until manually cleaned with the backend stopped; automatic transfer-artifact expiry is a follow-up.
